qs.q: Suppose $y=Ce^{mx}$ is a solution of the differential equation \[ y''+y'-6y=0. \] If $y(0)=2$ and $\lim_{x\to\infty} y(x)=0$, then $y$ is
hints: Substituting an exponential $y=Ce^{mx}$ into the equation gives an equation for $m$.
Compute $y'$ and $y''$ for $y=Ce^{mx}$, substitute, and divide by $Ce^{mx}$.
Substituting $y=e^{rx}$ into $ay''+by'+cy=0$ gives the characteristic equation $ar^2+br+c=0$; $e^{rx}\to0$ as $x\to\infty$ only when $r<0$, and $y(0)=C$ for $y=Ce^{rx}$.

qs.q: A particle moves along a straight line with acceleration \[ a(t)=\frac{1}{t^2}, \qquad t>0. \] If $s(t)$ denotes the position of the particle, $s(1)=0$, and $s'(1)=1$, then $s(t)$ is
hints: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, and velocity is the derivative of position, so integrate twice.
Integrate $a(t)$ once to get $v(t)=s'(t)$ and use $s'(1)=1$ to find the first constant.
$v(t)=\int a(t)\,dt+C_1$ and $s(t)=\int v(t)\,dt+C_2$, using $\int t^n\,dt=\dfrac{t^{n+1}}{n+1}$ for $n\neq-1$ and $\int t^{-1}\,dt=\ln t$ for $t>0$.

qs.q: The solution of the initial-value problem \[ \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1+\sin x}{y-1}, \qquad y(0)=2, \] is
hints: The right side is a function of $x$ times a function of $y$, so the equation is separable.
Move every $y$ factor to the side with $dy$ and every $x$ factor to the side with $dx$, then integrate both sides.
For $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{g(x)}{f(y)}$: $\int f(y)\,dy=\int g(x)\,dx+C$. Use the initial condition for $C$, and when taking a square root choose the sign that fits the initial value.

qs.q: A hot cup of coffee is placed in a room whose temperature is $25^\circ\text{C}$. The temperature of the coffee is initially $85^\circ\text{C}$, and after 10 minutes it is $55^\circ\text{C}$. Using Newton's law of cooling, the temperature $T(t)$ after $t$ minutes is
hints: Newton's law of cooling says the temperature difference $T-A$ from the room decays exponentially.
Write the general cooling solution using the room and initial temperatures, then use the 10-minute reading to find the decay factor.
Newton's law gives $T(t)=A+(T_0-A)e^{-kt}$, and for any fixed time $t_1$, $e^{-kt}=\left(e^{-kt_1}\right)^{t/t_1}$.

qs.q: The solution of the initial-value problem \[ (x^2+1)y'+2xy=xe^x, \qquad y(0)=1 \] is
hints: This is a first-order linear equation in $y$.
Divide by $x^2+1$ to get the form $y'+P(x)y=Q(x)$ and find the integrating factor.
$\rho=e^{\int P\,dx}$ and $(\rho y)'=\rho Q$; integration by parts is $\int u\,dv=uv-\int v\,du$.

qs.q: A one-parameter family of solutions of the differential equation \[ y'=-4x^2+4xy-y^2+2 \] is given by
hints: The right side depends on $x$ and $y$ only through one linear combination, so use a substitution $v=ax+by$.
Collect the quadratic terms into a perfect square of a linear expression in $x$ and $y$, and let $v$ be that expression.
With $v=ax+by+c$, $v'=a+by'$; the equation becomes $v'=f(v)$, which is separable: $\int\dfrac{dv}{f(v)}=\int dx$.

qs.q: A general nonzero solution of the differential equation \[ x^2y'=xy+3y^2 \] is
hints: Every term has the same total degree in $x$ and $y$, so the equation is homogeneous.
Divide by $x^2$ to write $y'$ as a function of $y/x$, then substitute $v=y/x$.
With $v=\dfrac yx$: $y=vx$ and $y'=v+xv'$; the resulting equation in $v$ and $x$ is separable.

qs.q: By an appropriate substitution, the Bernoulli equation \[ x\sqrt[3]{y^2}\,y'+5\sqrt[3]{y^5}=x^3 \] can be transformed into the linear equation
hints: Write the equation in the Bernoulli form $y'+P(x)y=Q(x)y^n$ and identify $n$.
Divide by the coefficient of $y'$ to reach the standard Bernoulli form, then substitute $v=y^{1-n}$.
For $y'+Py=Qy^n$, the substitution $v=y^{1-n}$ gives $v'=(1-n)y^{-n}y'$, which turns the equation into a linear one in $v$.

qs.q: A general nonzero solution of the differential equation \[ 2xy'+y^3e^{-2x}=2xy \] is given by
hints: Besides the linear terms the equation has a $y^3$ term, so it is a Bernoulli equation.
Divide by the coefficient of $y'$ and rearrange to reach $y'+P(x)y=Q(x)y^n$, then substitute $v=y^{1-n}$.
$v=y^{1-n}$ gives $v'=(1-n)y^{-n}y'$; solve the resulting linear equation with $\rho=e^{\int P\,dx}$.

qs.q: If $k(0)=2$ and the differential equation \[ \left(2y\cos 2x+5x^4y^2\right)dx+\left(k(x)+2x^5y\right)dy=0 \] is exact, then $k(x)$ is
hints: Use the test for exactness of $M\,dx+N\,dy=0$.
Compute $\partial M/\partial y$ and $\partial N/\partial x$ and set them equal.
$M\,dx+N\,dy=0$ is exact if and only if $M_y=N_x$; integrate the resulting $k'(x)$ and use the given value of $k(0)$ for the constant.

qs.q: The general solution of the differential equation \[ \left(x^3+\frac{y}{x}\right)dx+\left(y^2+\ln x\right)dy=0 \] is
hints: Check whether the equation is exact.
Compare $\partial M/\partial y$ with $\partial N/\partial x$, then integrate $M$ with respect to $x$ to start building $F(x,y)$.
If $M_y=N_x$, then $F=\int M\,dx+g(y)$ with $F_y=N$, and the solution is $F(x,y)=C$.

qs.q: If a nonconstant solution of the differential equation \[ yy''=(y')^2+y' \] has tangent line $y=2x+1$ at $x=0$, then the solution is given by
hints: The independent variable $x$ does not appear, so this is a reducible second-order equation with $x$ missing.
Read off $y(0)$ and $y'(0)$ from the tangent line, then set $p=y'$ with $y''=p\,\dfrac{dp}{dy}$.
With $x$ missing, set $p=y'$ and $y''=p\dfrac{dp}{dy}$. A tangent line $y=mx+b$ at $x=x_0$ means $y(x_0)=mx_0+b$ and $y'(x_0)=m$.

qs.q: If \[ a\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}+b\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\end{bmatrix}+c\begin{bmatrix}-1\\0\end{bmatrix}+d\begin{bmatrix}0\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\end{bmatrix}, \] and every solution $(a,b,c,d)$ can be written in the form \[ s(1,0,p,q)+t(0,1,r,l), \] then the value of $\dfrac{p+r}{q+l}$ is
hints: The vector equation is a homogeneous linear system in $a,b,c,d$.
Write the two component equations and solve them for $c$ and $d$ in terms of $a$ and $b$.
In a solution written as $s\mathbf{u}+t\mathbf{w}$, the variables whose entries are $1,0$ and $0,1$ are the free variables; express the other variables in terms of them and read off the vectors.

qs.q: Which one of the following subsets is a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^4$?
opts: The set of all vectors $(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$ such that $x_1+x_2+x_3=0$ and $2x_2-x_4=0$
The set of all vectors $(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$ such that $x_1^2+x_2=0$
The set of all vectors $(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$ such that $x_1-3x_2+x_4=2$
The set of all vectors $(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$ such that $x_1\le x_2$
The set of all vectors $(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$ such that $x_1x_4=0$
hints: A subset is a subspace when it contains $\mathbf{0}$ and is closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
Check each set for the zero vector first, then look for a pair of vectors or a scalar that breaks closure.
The solution set of a homogeneous linear system $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ is always a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
steps: $x_1+x_2+x_3=0,\ 2x_2-x_4=0$ is a homogeneous linear system, so its solution set contains $\mathbf{0}$ and is closed under sums and scalar multiples: a subspace.
$x_1-3x_2+x_4=2$: the zero vector gives $0\neq2$, so $\mathbf{0}$ is not in it.
$x_1\le x_2$: $(0,1,0,0)$ is in it, but $-1\cdot(0,1,0,0)$ would need $0\le-1$.
$x_1x_4=0$: $(1,0,0,0)$ and $(0,0,0,1)$ are in it, but their sum has $x_1x_4=1$.
qs.brief: Only the homogeneous linear system $x_1+x_2+x_3=0,\ 2x_2-x_4=0$ gives a subspace.

qs.q: The vectors $u=(1,0,k)$, $v=(0,1,1)$, and $w=(4-k,1,4)$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ are linearly independent when
hints: Three vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$ are independent exactly when the matrix built from them is invertible.
Put $u$, $v$, $w$ as the rows (or columns) of a $3\times3$ matrix and compute its determinant as a function of $k$.
$n$ vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ are linearly independent if and only if the matrix having them as columns (or rows) has nonzero determinant.
steps: Take $\det\begin{bmatrix}1&0&k\\0&1&1\\4-k&1&4\end{bmatrix}$ and expand along the first row.
The determinant is nonzero, so the vectors are independent, exactly when $k\neq1,3$.
